# Practice for Session 4 {#sec-s4-practice}

These questions mix all topics of the session, in the style of the entry quiz and the exam. Before you calculate, write down what is paid when, and ask yourself whether you are moving money forward or back in time. Questions marked ★ are a little harder.

::: {.callout-tip}
## 1. An overdraft for a few weeks
Loop Cycles uses its overdraft of €3,600 for 45 days at 9 % a year (simple interest, 365 days). How much interest does it pay?

::: {.hidden-solution}
$3\,600 \cdot 0.09 \cdot \frac{45}{365} \approx 39.95$ euros.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## 2. The rate behind an investment
€8,000 grew to €9,277.55 in 6 years with compound interest. What was the yearly rate?

::: {.hidden-solution}
$i = \left(\frac{9\,277.55}{8\,000}\right)^{1/6} - 1 = 1.15969^{1/6} - 1 \approx 0.025$, so **2.5 %**.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## 3. Comparing two loan offers
Bank A charges a nominal 4.8 % a year with monthly interest. Bank B charges 4.9 % with yearly interest. Which loan is cheaper?

::: {.hidden-solution}
Bank A: $\left(1 + \frac{0.048}{12}\right)^{12} - 1 = 1.004^{12} - 1 \approx 4.91\,\%$. Bank B: 4.90 %. Bank B is (slightly) cheaper, even though its nominal rate is higher.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## 4. Pay now or in instalments?
A used delivery van costs €18,000 cash, or three payments of €6,500 at the end of each of the next three years. Your money earns 4 %. Which is cheaper?

::: {.hidden-solution}
Present value of the instalments: $6\,500 \cdot \frac{1 - 1.04^{-3}}{0.04} = 6\,500 \cdot 2.775091 \approx 18\,038.09$ euros. Paying cash (€18,000) is cheaper, by about €38 in today's money. The instalments add up to €19,500, but that number is not the right comparison.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## 5. How much to save
Loop Cycles wants €15,000 in 6 years for a second van. How much must it save at the end of each year at 3 %?

::: {.hidden-solution}
Solve $15\,000 = R \cdot \frac{1.03^6 - 1}{0.03}$ for $R$: $R = \frac{15\,000 \cdot 0.03}{1.03^6 - 1} = \frac{450}{0.194052} \approx 2\,318.96$ euros a year.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## 6. A monthly loan
A loan of €8,000 at a nominal 7.2 % a year is repaid in 24 monthly instalments. Calculate the instalment and the total interest.

::: {.hidden-solution}
Monthly rate $\frac{0.072}{12} = 0.006$. $A = 8\,000 \cdot \frac{0.006 \cdot 1.006^{24}}{1.006^{24} - 1} \approx 358.91$ euros a month. Total interest: $24 \cdot 358.91 - 8\,000 \approx 613.75$ euros.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## 7. Paying off a loan early
A loan of €50,000 at 4 % is repaid in 10 equal yearly instalments. Calculate the instalment and the remaining debt after 5 years.

::: {.hidden-solution}
$A = 50\,000 \cdot \frac{0.04 \cdot 1.04^{10}}{1.04^{10} - 1} \approx 6\,164.55$ euros.

$K_5 = 50\,000 \cdot 1.04^5 - 6\,164.55 \cdot \frac{1.04^5 - 1}{0.04} \approx 60\,832.65 - 33\,389.18 \approx 27\,443.47$ euros.

After half the time, more than half the debt is still there, because the early instalments are mostly interest.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## 8. Does it pay off?
A fleet of cargo bikes for deliveries costs €50,000 and brings in €15,000 at the end of each year for 4 years, with no value at the end. Calculate the NPV at 8 % and at 6 %. What do you conclude?

::: {.hidden-solution}
At 8 %: $-50\,000 + 15\,000 \cdot \frac{1 - 1.08^{-4}}{0.08} = -50\,000 + 15\,000 \cdot 3.312127 \approx -318.10$ euros.

At 6 %: $-50\,000 + 15\,000 \cdot 3.465106 \approx 1\,976.58$ euros.

The investment pays off if money costs 6 %, but not if it costs 8 %. Its internal rate of return lies between the two (about 7.7 %).
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## 9. ★ How long until the loan is paid off?
Loop Cycles borrows €10,000 at 5 % and can afford €1,500 a year. How many instalments does it need?

::: {.hidden-solution}
Set the present value of the instalments equal to the loan, $10\,000 = 1\,500 \cdot \frac{1 - 1.05^{-n}}{0.05}$, and solve for $n$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
1 - 1.05^{-n} &= \frac{10\,000 \cdot 0.05}{1\,500} = \frac{1}{3}\\
1.05^{-n} &= \frac{2}{3}\\
n &= \frac{\ln(1.5)}{\ln(1.05)} \approx 8.31
\end{aligned}
$$

It needs 8 full instalments and a smaller ninth one (about €473).
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## 10. ★ When does declining balance fall behind?
Equipment for €20,000 has a useful life of 5 years. Compare straight-line depreciation with 30 % declining balance. In which year is the declining-balance amount smaller than the straight-line amount for the first time?

::: {.hidden-solution}
Straight-line: €4,000 every year. Declining balance: year 1: $0.3 \cdot 20\,000 = 6\,000$; year 2: $0.3 \cdot 14\,000 = 4\,200$; year 3: $0.3 \cdot 9\,800 = 2\,940$. From **year 3** on, declining balance writes off less.
:::
:::
